decisions.reason: Selecting a satin finish and champagne-gold distribution that includes the É accent does not change the accent's locked geometry, derivation, alignment, or revision policy.
The source message's composition impact is already represented by the candidate's same-message kerning MODIFY and RESUME; the material preference adds no further composition-state change.
Applying champagne gold to the second V's right arm changes its material treatment, not the second V's form, construction method, hierarchy, alignment, or role.
The selected finish and color placement do not alter the approved Hero V geometry or its locked structural constraints.
The satin treatment is preferred because it supports the existing warmth, depth, luxury, and hierarchy goals; it does not change those broader brand-expression requirements.
The material selection does not change the custom construction, proportions, architectural language, or fixed-asset boundary of the internal letterforms.
Champagne-gold placement on the three signature elements does not modify their shared terminal geometry or terminal-expression rules.
The finish and distribution preference does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
A preferred but not yet finalized material direction does not change the production-ready artwork deliverable or establish a new export requirement.
